Funny it came to discussion again these days. I've always read about
it, but never was a direct victim of a similar case.
nobody ever heard any proposal, but we had a tournament yesterday at a
local cards convention and, in first round, I seated with another 4
vote or anti-votes deck (me, toreador with obf -> ventrue -> !ventrue
with Quentin -> Justicars and Inner Circles -> !ventrue with potence).
Of course it was a very complicated table to manage during vote
counting, but I got Michael Luther and some princes, so I was the
least affected by Quentin's special (he could cancel only 2 votes from
me, and I got the opportunity of getting votes from a Inner Circle
after it if it was me calling the referendum).

But at the very first KRC I've called, the !Ventrue with Quentin
played a Delaying Tactics - this on a vote that would harm his
predator by 3 pool when he already had around 20 and a Inner Circle
ready, and in a table with 5 heavy titled decks, including its own
prey! It made clear that my prey and grand-prey had some sort of
non-aggression pact - and as the !Ventrue gained his first VP and
played Gambit Accepted, there were no doubt that they would manage to
stand ground for the two to survive until they get head-to-head and
see what happens.

I survived with the two, and the very first political action for my
prey (around 15 pool) when that happened was to play a KRC with 3 for
me (with less than 10 pool) and 1 for my grandprey (with around 20).
Of course some prize splitting was involved - why would someone let
his prey make at least 2 VPs just to try to oust them and gain the GW
with the VP "forfeit" of Gambit Accepted?

(As a side note, this Delaying Tactics was played after all vote
counting and when I played Voter Captivation. I've read again the card
texts as soon as I could when the round was over, and Voter says:
"usable AFTER a successfull referendum", while Delaying says "usable
DURING a referendum". I recall I asked two or three times after vote
counting: "so it has passed? it's X votes for and X-5 against?" before
playing the Voter, and after it my grandprey played Delaying Tactics.
It isn't the correct timing, is it? Since it was declared the
referendum passed and a Voter was played, he could not play Delaying
anymore, right?)

cheers

the_capuchin

LSJ <vte...@white-wolf.com> wrote in message news:<3F8940DC...@white-wolf.com>...

I don't understand the rules. Why do we use the phrase
"sportsmanlike conduct" in the tournament rules, when we really mean a
defined set of play-to-win rules (nothing more, nothing less)? Can we
*please* change the rules to say what they really mean, instead of
some easily misinterpretted phrase like "sportsmanlike conduct" ?

Almost all other things in our game use precise language; I think we
should continue that excellent pattern and clarify the rules. I
understand the necessity of using the phrase, "reasonable chance to
win," but that's as vague as I can understand.

Just to be entirely clear, this is what "sportsmanlike conduct" means
in the tournament rules:

1) A player must try to obtain the game win.
2) If a player has no reasonable chance of a game win, he must try to
maximize his VPs.
3) If the player has no reasonable chance of getting more than zero
VPs (or he has already obtained the game win), he may play however he
wants (including self-ousting, giving away VPs, etc.)

"Reasonable chance" is defined by the judge. I personally use 5% as
a ballpark figure.

Also, the above doesn't mention anything about preventing other
people from getting the game win. Consider this crazy example:

Down to a two player game. Player A has 0 VPs, an empty library, and
one vampire. Player B has 1 VP, an empty library, no hand, an empty
crypt, no minions, and 30 pool. There are 15 seconds left in the
round.

Player A can attempt to withdraw (and surely succeed), thus getting 1
VP, and allowing player B to get the game win. Or, player A can
simply prevent player B from withdrawing, but time will run out before
player A can oust player B, thereby preventing B from a game win, but
only getting 1/2 VP.

Is it legal for A to not go for the full VP to prevent B from getting
the Game Win? If so, could LSJ state rule 2a above?

Thanks,

Ira

Messages.Author: DeistMutts
Messages.Body:
I don't want any ppl freaking out about my comment, but this comment
is purely from my personal playing experience over the year. So if you
have any suggestions positive to bring up, I'd gladly respond.. :)

Ppl will propose "illegal deals" and MAKE it look as if it's legal.
Ppl will also argue that they WERE trying to make a deal that's in the
"best interest" in winning the game, but then "something ELSE happens"
and changed it. Ppl will also argue that the deal IS legal if
'fantasizing' what your next move is.

I personally all but give up on whining about deals other ppl make
during the game that I personally believe it's illegal, and there are
those that believe my whining about such thing was invalid cuz 'blah
blah blah, excuses, excuses, excuses'. So, a good friend told me once
"So what's your point?" and I realized he was right.. There's nothing
I can do unless I have solid proof and even so, I would basically ruin
the game for everyone else on the table while trying to show solid
proof with the rulebook.

So what's the point of this? Just attack the person who's trying to
hurt you the most, ESPECIALLY if he's an ally (casting silly parity
shifts on you, etc). If you truly believe your prey or predator making
the deals/moves against you is purely personal/evil/illegal, just
announce to the table that they shouldn't worry about you and you're
going after your prey or predator solely and don't care about game
anymore just to teach that person a harsh lession to play the game
next time. Afterall, it IS just a game, even at tournaments. It works
somewhat for me, better than whining and asking for judges and make
yourself look bad if the player comes up with lame excuses that seems
legit.

Orpheus, I'll give you one example.. how many ppl were playing
Giovannis at this past storyline tournaments worldwide? Don't you
think someone might JUST make some "illegal" deals just to get other
giovannis on the same table some advantage? Excuse? "Need to make
Giovannis into the finals and win the tournament just for the story
purpose" Can you argue with that? And will ANYONE admit to it? :)

---DeistMutts---

Messages.Author: Timlagor
Messages.Body:
hawk_the_demon expounded:


"reasonable chance" could be interpreted as anything from 1% to about
40% depending on the player -I think most people could tell the
difference between these two cases.
"Reasonable" is totally subjective whereas "around 5%" is just a
judgement of the game state -obviously you make a judgement based on
your knowlegde of the game and the information you have about people's
decks.

To put it another (perhaps clearer) way:

5%: you have to estimate how likely you are to be able to win
'reasonable': you have to estimate how likely you are to win THEN decide
if that constittutes are reasonable chance.

Some people find it useful to have a figure in mind. No one claimed they
could calculate these probabilities precisely.

Hey All,

> Because we don't mean nothing more than that set.

Oh! I didn't realize that. Are the other things enumerable, and if
so, could someone enumerate them for me?

> Who feeds you the equations to compute such percentages from a given

:) Of course there are no equations. My method is to mentally assume
infinite alternate universes where the game plays out in a variety of
ways. "Reasonable chances" are defined by the aggregate outcome from
all those alternate universes.

While any number is uncomputable by a formula, I think it's better
than nothing.

allow B to get the Game Win?

Messages.Author: hawk_the_demon
Messages.Body:
> Some people find it useful to have a figure in mind. No one claimed they
> could calculate these probabilities precisely.

true, but this figure is IMO useless in this case unless you have
something to base your rough calculations on.

you have to make assumtions to base your rough estimate on, and since
you control the assumtions, you can control the result of your
calculation. would your assumptions be the same if you are already in
the final?

so:

5%: you have to estimate how likely you are to be able to win using an
estimation where you have a very good control over the result and
compare this to a fixed number that has no meaning.

'reasonable': you have to estimate if you have a reasonable chance of
getting more VP's.

You're intentionally ignoring the point that they judge cannot declare
legal play to be illegal without violating the precepts of his position.

Yes, the judge could eject a player for dealing seven library cards to
his hand to start the game. But that would mean, of course, that, when
the gross misconduct of the judge is revealed, that the tournament is
unsanctioned.

players are bound by that decision at the tournament, but there is
recourse after the tournament that yields the result stated.

>
>You're intentionally ignoring the point that they judge cannot declare
>legal play to be illegal without violating the precepts of his position.
>
>Yes, the judge could eject a player for dealing seven library cards to

>his hand to start the game. ...

That's a silly example. The standard case which keeps coming up is an
action such as transferring out which is legal so far as the game's
mechanics are concerned but which may be held to be unsporting because
the player is not playing to win, say. One part of the rules allows
the player to take this action but the tournament rules override this.
So it is with bribery involving the prizes. If the judge decides
that, in the particular circumstances, this is unsporting then he is
empowered to rule the action illegal. And, as he is likely to have
consensus support from the players, his ruling is likely to stick.

Andrew
